title: Emerging Technologies Classification and Adoption Strategies (Module 8 deck)
author: Andres Fortino (course deck, user-supplied)
type: course analytical framework (reused from A7 register)
locator: Slides 26-35 classification; 38-47 adoption rules; 45 Rule #7 (know the required adoption style for your job); 54 Module 9 preview (Implementing Emerging Technologies: Proof of Concept, Task Technology Fit, Killer Uses, ECTM, FRS)
supports: Bleeding edge: extremely new, high risk from instability; leading edge: crossed the chasm. Rule #1 wait for the crossing before adopting; Rule #2 use pilot projects to test untested or underdeveloped technologies; Rule #7 know the adoption style your job requires. Module 9 (implementation) lists proof of concept and task-technology fit as implementation topics.
does_not_support: Readiness criteria for a specific organization; the Module 9 deck itself was not available to this agent.

title: Assignments 3-5 specialist outputs (Innovation and Disruption; Promethean; Diffusion)
author: Minghan Liu
type: upstream team-agent outputs (reused from A7 register)
supports: A3: compare staff-only, simple retrieval and the proposed agent before any pilot. A4: long-term significance carries Low weight on present decisions (incremental-counterfactual test). A5: FAQ chatbots in admissions are past take-off; tool-using recruitment agents are at innovators/early adopters (denominator rule).
does_not_support: Independent evidence; prior AI-assisted student analyses used as inputs.

title: Assignment 6 Emerging Technology Adoption Agent v1.1 outputs
author: Minghan Liu
type: upstream team-agent output (reused from A7 register)
supports: Agent-based applicant support is BLEEDING EDGE (Rule 1: no adopt; Rule 2: pilot). SPS: proof of concept now (staff-only vs Violet/simple retrieval vs agent on about 300 approved or synthetic inquiries), gated G1-G4 to a bounded experiment (at most 10% of web inquiries, 8 weeks, staff approve every message, no record writes, stop rule). G3 compliance sign-off; G4 approval capacity confirmed. Handoff: can admissions staff the human-approval and content-governance work?
does_not_support: Independent evidence; an AI-assisted student analysis used as the upstream input.

title: Assignment 7 Organizational Adoption (Readiness) Agent v1.1 outputs
author: Minghan Liu
supports: SPS: proof of concept READY WITH CONDITIONS; live bounded experiment NOT YET READY; most consequential gap = operating ownership; ACT-5 requires a privacy/compliance review of vendor terms. Handoff to Landscape: shortlist vendors only against data-terms requirements (no-training, retention, deletion, least-privilege connector).
does_not_support: Independent evidence; an AI-assisted student analysis used as the upstream input.

title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
author: Frank F. Xu et al. (CMU and others)
type: independent agent benchmark (reused from A4 register)
supports: The most competitive agent completed 30% of simulated workplace tasks autonomously; more difficult long-horizon tasks remain beyond current systems.
does_not_support: Current frontier performance after the tested models; production reliability. STALE-RISK: the 30% figure is the paper's own result for models available when it was written; see D35 for the refreshed leaderboard.

title: Gartner Predicts Over 40% of Agentic AI Projects Will Be Canceled by End of 2027
author: Gartner
type: analyst forecast and non-random poll (reused from A5 register)
supports: January 2025 poll of 3,412 webinar attendees: 19% significant agentic AI investment, 42% conservative, 31% wait-and-see; over 40% of agentic projects forecast to be cancelled by end-2027; only about 130 of thousands of 'agentic AI' vendors judged real ('agent washing'). Stated causes: 'escalating costs, unclear business value, and inadequate risk controls'; Gartner recommends 'only pursuing agentic AI in cases where it delivers clear value or ROI' (SD Times report, 2025-06-30, opened 2026-11-08).
does_not_support: Measured adoption; the poll is self-selected.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education (Ellucian 2026 AI report)
author: Ellucian
type: vendor survey (779 administrators, 300+ institutions, 93% U.S.) (reused from A5 register)
supports: Institutional AI use 66% (49% in 2024); 36% of Marketing, Admissions and Enrollment respondents use chatbots for FAQs; data security/privacy is the top institutional barrier (56%); 14% of executive respondents report a dedicated AI budget. No share for AI agents is reported.
does_not_support: Representativeness (vendor customers and contacts); agentic use.

title: Unity Environmental University taps Agentforce and Education Cloud
author: Salesforce
type: vendor customer story (reused from A5 register)
supports: A university planned to deploy recruitment agents on its website to answer prospective-student questions, handle requests for information and guide applications, with hand-off to staff; it expected to save $800 of staff time per web RFI.
does_not_support: Measured results; the deployment was planned at publication and the savings are a projection.

title: Agentforce for Education: Recruitment and Admissions pre-built skill; Dreamforce 2025 education keynote summary
author: Salesforce; Cloud for Good (partner)
type: vendor product page and partner summary (reused from A5 register)
supports: A pre-built recruitment/admissions agent skill exists (answer questions from knowledge articles, create information requests, register campus tours, start applications); partner summary lists recruitment and RFI skills as generally available with some items in beta. This is change-agent activity that raises trialability.
does_not_support: Customer counts or outcomes; the product page itself warns features 'may not be currently available'.

title: Meet the NYUAdmissionsBot
author: NYU Admissions
type: organization primary source (reused from A7 register)
supports: NYU Admissions offers a generative AI admissions bot on its admissions site and applicant portal, available 24/7; it hands off to a live agent or a contact form when it cannot answer.
does_not_support: SPS graduate admissions specifically; agentic actions; vendor; usage.

title: NYU SPS Graduate Admissions
author: NYU School of Professional Studies
type: organization primary source (reused from A7 register)
supports: Phone/email contact, weekday appointments, information sessions and 'For immediate assistance, try our chatbot, Violet.'
does_not_support: Violet's architecture, tool use, vendor or usage.

title: Salesforce Introduces New Flexible Agentforce Pricing
author: Salesforce
type: vendor pricing announcement (reused from A6 register)
supports: Flex Credits: an agent action consumes 20 credits ($0.10 per action); packs of 100,000 credits cost $500; earlier conversational pricing was $2 per conversation; per-user licences were announced for later availability.
does_not_support: Total cost of ownership (integration, review, monitoring, correction) or current negotiated prices; one vendor only.

title: The AI Act implementation timeline: What changes under the AI Omnibus?
author: Future of Privacy Forum
type: secondary legal analysis (reused from A6 register)
supports: The AI Omnibus (published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026) moves Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 instead of 2 August 2026; Article 50 transparency obligations became generally applicable on 2 August 2026.
does_not_support: Whether a particular SPS use is in scope; any U.S. law. Legal determinations belong to compliance.

title: AI Act Service Desk: Education and vocational training (Annex III point 3)
author: European Commission AI Act Service Desk
type: official regulatory guidance page (reused from A6 register)
supports: High-risk education uses include AI systems intended to determine access or admission, or to assign persons to education institutions (3a), to evaluate learning outcomes (3b), to assess the appropriate level of education (3c), and to monitor prohibited student behaviour (3d).
does_not_support: Whether an applicant-support agent that excludes admission decisions is in scope; that depends on design and intended purpose and requires legal review.

title: Guidelines on transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems (Article 50 AI Act)
author: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
supports: 'Article 50 of the AI Act applies from 2 August 2026.' People must be informed when they interact directly with an AI system; the Commission guidelines are meant to help providers, deployers and authorities comply.
does_not_support: Whether a particular university is a provider or deployer, or in scope; the guidelines' legal status. Legal determinations belong to counsel.

title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
author: Shunyu Yao, Noah Shinn, Pedram Razavi, Karthik Narasimhan
supports: Peer-reviewed benchmark of multi-turn, policy-bound customer-service tasks with tools: 'even state-of-the-art function calling agents (gpt-4o) succeed on <50% of the tasks, and are terribly inconsistent (pass^8 < 25% in retail)'.
does_not_support: Current models (results are for 2024 models); admissions tasks. Created by researchers associated with an agent vendor (Sierra), but peer-reviewed.

title: TheAgentCompany leaderboard (Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub data, mirrored by BenchLeader)
author: Epoch AI data; BenchLeader mirror
date: Data as of 2026-11-15; newest listed model published 2025-09-29
supports: Share of tasks resolved: DeepSeek V3.2 42.9% (model published 2025-09-29); Gemini 2.5 Flash 41.1%; Claude Sonnet 4 33.1%; Claude 3.7 Sonnet 30.9%; Gemini 2.5 Pro 30.3%; Claude 3.5 Sonnet 24.0%; GPT-4o 8.6%. Results depend on the harness; the environment is simulated.
does_not_support: Frontier models released after September 2025 (not listed, so the board itself lags); whether results were independently re-run; admissions tasks.

title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity (METR), as reported by Simon Willison
author: METR; Simon Willison (report)
locator: Blog summary of the randomized study (METR paper linked)
supports: Randomized trial: 16 experienced open-source developers, about 15 issues each from their own repositories. 'when developers use AI tools, they take 19% longer than without'. Developers forecast a 24% speed-up and afterwards believed AI had reduced completion time by 20%.
does_not_support: Newer tools or less experienced developers; small sample. Read via a secondary summary; the METR page itself could not be opened from this workspace.

title: Developers remain willing but reluctant to use AI: the 2025 Developer Survey results are here
author: Stack Overflow
supports: 49,000+ respondents; 80% of developers use AI tools in their workflows; trust in AI accuracy fell from 40% to 29%; on whether the AI-agent revolution is here, the answer is 'not yet', although 52% say agents have affected how they work.
does_not_support: A representative sample (self-selected); admissions.

title: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
author: Linux Foundation
supports: Founding projects: Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP), Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md, under 'a neutral, open foundation'. Platinum members include AWS, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI. Self-reported adoption: 'more than 10,000 published MCP servers'; AGENTS.md in 'more than 60,000 open source projects'.
does_not_support: That a given admissions vendor supports MCP; security of MCP servers; independent adoption counts.

title: Salesforce launches AI agent at Unity Environmental University
author: GovTech (Government Technology)
supports: Unity Environmental University launched 'Una', an Agentforce agent that helps prospective students through the application process and matches them with programs. 'Salesforce estimates Una will save recruiters 17 hours per week.' No measured results reported; other colleges (Knox, Berry) are said to use AI agents for recruitment.
does_not_support: Measured outcomes (the 17 hours is a vendor estimate); human review arrangements.

title: University of Nottingham Malaysia deploys Agentforce to create a seamless experience for prospective students
author: Salesforce (press release)
supports: The agent answers prospective-student questions (entry requirements, fees, scholarships, accommodation) at any hour and lets students book advisor calls or campus tours ('self-schedule in seconds'). Outcomes (faster responses, higher conversion, satisfaction) are stated as aims; no measured results are given.
does_not_support: Measured outcomes; independent confirmation.

title: Element451 launches Bolt as the AI agent platform for higher education; How higher-ed teams reclaimed 67+ work years with AI agents
author: Element451 (vendor blog/press)
date: Bolt announcement 2026-05-28 (updated 2026-11-11); '67+ work years' post updated 2025-12-17
supports: Bolt agents answer inquiries, run outreach and, at one college, 'evaluated and processed incoming applications'; integrations with Slate, Salesforce, Banner and Workday. Vendor claims '11.8 million minutes saved in a single year', 'equivalent to more than 67 full-time work years'. No calculation, institution count or independent verification is given, and 11.8 million minutes is about 196,700 hours, or about 95 work-years at 2,080 hours per year, so the stated 67 does not reconcile on a standard work year.
does_not_support: Any measured outcome usable for a decision; human-approval controls (not described).

title: The state of AI (2026 survey)
author: McKinsey & Company
supports: 40% of respondents from large organizations (over $1 billion revenue) report scaling AI agents, up from 27%; 22% of smaller organizations; agents are scaled most often 'within IT, knowledge management, and software engineering'; 37% attribute at least some EBIT impact to AI.
does_not_support: Higher education or admissions; causation (self-reported).

title: Gartner Predicts 40% of Enterprise Apps Will Feature Task-Specific AI Agents by 2026, Up from Less Than 5% in 2025
author: Gartner (press release)
supports: Forecast: 40% of enterprise apps will feature task-specific AI agents by 2026; best case, agentic AI 'could drive approximately 30% of enterprise application software revenue by 2035', 'surpassing $450 billion'.
does_not_support: Measured adoption; any specific application. A forecast: popular, never decision-driving.

title: The Impact of AI on Work in Higher Education
author: EDUCAUSE (Jenay Robert)
supports: 94% of higher-ed respondents used AI tools for work in the past six months; only 54% are aware of work-related AI policies or guidelines; 38% see 'creating tools for student services' as an opportunity; 6% use AI for application screening. The report contains no findings on AI agents.
does_not_support: Agent adoption in admissions (not measured), a representative institutional rate.

title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026 edition), as summarized by Giskard
author: OWASP GenAI Security Project; Giskard summary
supports: Community security taxonomy for agents: ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack; ASI02 Tool Misuse and Exploitation; ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse; ASI04 Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities; ASI05 Unexpected Code Execution; ASI06 Memory & Context Poisoning; ASI07 Insecure Inter-Agent Communication; ASI08 Cascading Failures; ASI09 Human-Agent Trust Exploitation; ASI10 Rogue Agents.
does_not_support: Legal requirements; incidence rates. Read via a secondary summary.

title: LLM inference prices have fallen rapidly but unequally across tasks
author: Epoch AI (Cottier, Snodin, Owen, Adamczewski)
supports: The price to reach a given performance level fell at rates 'ranging from 9x to 900x per year' depending on the milestone; the fastest drops were recent and may not persist.
does_not_support: Total cost of an agent workflow (agents use many calls; review time dominates in human-approved designs); negotiated prices.

title: GDPR Article 22: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
author: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, reproduced by gdpr-text.com
supports: A data subject has 'the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing ... which produces legal effects concerning him or her or similarly significantly affects him or her', with exceptions (contract, law, explicit consent) and safeguards including 'the right to obtain human intervention'.
does_not_support: Whether any specific admissions workflow is in scope; legal conclusions (counsel).

title: SWE-bench Verified leaderboard (BenchLM aggregator)
author: BenchLM.ai
supports: Top listed scores are 88.6% to 96%, all self-reported by model vendors; the aggregator states none of its 118 results was run independently and marks the benchmark as saturated and contaminated ('display-only').
does_not_support: Real-world coding productivity; any independent measurement. An aggregator of vendor self-reports.

title: NYU SPS graduate application site (go.grad.sps.nyu.edu/apply)
author: NYU School of Professional Studies
supports: The application site footer says: 'Chat with our friendly virtual assistant, Violet, who's ready to help!' The page does not name the application or CRM platform.
does_not_support: Which vendor runs Violet or the CRM; Violet's capabilities or performance.
